title: Oulun Tilapalvelut - Paineilmalaitteiden huolto- ja korjauspalvelut
description: Oulun Tilapalvelut - Paineilmalaitteiden huolto- ja korjauspalvelut Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos hakee tällä tarjouspyynnöllä palveluntuottajaa toteuttamaan hallinnoimiensa kiinteistöjen paineilmalaitteiden (ilmakompressorit) huolto- ja korjauspalveluita. Tarkemmat tiedot hankinnan kuvauksesta, vaatimuksista ja tarjoushintojen antamisesta, vertailusta ja valinnasta löytyvät tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 0. Puitejärjestelyn kesto on 01.12.2026 - 30.11.2028. Sopimusta on mahdollista jatkaa kahdella optiokaudella (1.12.2028 - 30.11.2029 ja 1.12.2029 - 30.11.2030). Mikäli Tilaaja ei erikseen ilmoita halustaan luopua sopimuksesta viimeistään kolme (3) kuukautta ennen varsinaisen sopimuskauden tai ensimmäisen optiokauden päättymistä, sopimus jatkuu automaattisesti seuraavalle optiokaudelle. Tarjottaviin hintoihin tulee sisällyttää kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta tulevat kulut, jotka sisältävät mahdolliset kilometri, matka-, majoitus-, päiväraha-, ylityö- sekä toimitus-, laskutus- ja toimistokulut, työkalut, jätemaksut ja pientarvikelisät mukaan lukien. Kuitenkin niin, että korjaustyön tuntilaskutus tilattuun kohteeseen alkaa Oulun alueen rajalta tai toimipisteeltä Oulun alueen sisällä (matka-aika). Laskutusyksikkö 30 min. Sopimusta voivat hyödyntää myös muut Oulun kaupungin hallintokunnat / liikelaitokset, joilla on sama Y-tunnus, kuten Oulun vesi, Oulun Kaupunkiympäristöpalvelu ja Sivistys- ja kulttuuripalvelut. Indeksiehto. Katso sopimusluonnos kohta 14. Palvelussa noudatetaan JYSE 2025 mukaisia sopimusehtoja.,

title: Directed Faith Community Reintegration Project – Muslim Initiative
description: Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) Directed Faith Community Reintegration Project – Muslim Initiative This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Areas and the Edmonton area. Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: Compliant bid with the highest combined score of technical merit and price. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to provide Directed Faith Community Reintegration services in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Areas and the Edmonton area. Faith Community Reintegration Projects (FCRPs) support successful offender reintegration following their release from CSC institutions. Directed Faith Community Reintegration Projects (DFCRPs) are a specialized extension of FCRPs that align with CSC’s public safety mandate by supporting the reintegration of offenders from traditionally underserved faith communities. DFCRPs link offender reintegration goals to the mandates of organizations from traditionally underserved faith communities that are prepared to offer religious and spiritual services to offenders after release. DFCRPs support offender reintegration plans and program goals, by providing a range of services and activities that facilitate the transition and reintegration of individuals back into the community. These projects are designed to meet the unique religious and spiritual needs of specific groups, helping ensure that everyone has access to meaningful support on their reintegration journey. Communities of faith typically offer many diverse, faith-based, pro-social activities to the public that foster a sense of belonging while contributing to spiritual and religious growth. Offender involvement in these activities offers a direct means of addressing and mitigating risk factors linked to reoffending. DFCRPs facilitate and support the unique contribution of faith communities toward a holistic approach to safe and restorative reintegration practices. Objectives: To support successful offender reintegration following release from CSC institutions by: • Developing faith community capacity to engage with offenders; • Building bridges between offenders and their religious and spiritual community groups; • Liaising with parole and justice organizations, and faith communities; • Supporting offender reintegration plans and program goals; and • Assisting offenders to become contributing members of society. CSC may award up to two (2) contracts as a result of this Request for Proposal (RFP), one contract per STREAM. Stream 1 – Greater Toronto and Hamilton Areas Stream 2 – Edmonton Area Bidders may submit a proposal for one or both STREAMS. However, Bidders submitting a bid for both STREAMS must be able to provide sufficient services and resources, to meet CSC’s requirements for all the location(s) listed within the identified stream. Deliverables: The Contractor must submit the following to the Project Authority: 1. a copy of the disengagement model being used no later than six (6) months after contract award; 2. a copy of the monthly quantitative indicator reports and invoices no later than thirty (30) days after the end of the month during which the Contractor delivered the services; 3. a copy of the quarterly qualitative reports no later than thirty (30) days after the end of each quarterly reporting period. The monthly quantitative indicator reporting and quarterly qualitative reporting documents are attached in Annex F. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of date of Contract Award to March 31, 2028, with the option to renew for five (5) additional one-year periods. File Number: 21120-27-5405982 Contracting Authority: Mbinwi Ghogomu Telephone number: 343-549-7179 E-mail: Mbinwi.Ghogomu@csc-scc.gc.ca NOTE TO BIDDERS: Bidders can obtain the complete statement of work and evaluation criteria by downloading the solicitation document and associated documents from the Canada buys / tender opportunities website. The Crown reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada (English or French). After contract award, bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days of receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. This specification applies only to maintenance, inspection, testing, and reporting activities. No fabrication, building modifications, or new installation work are included within the scope.

title: Provide Preparator Services for an artifact collection in the care of Parks Canada

Work performed will ensure items are protected and compliant with conservation, handling, and transport standards. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE The period of the Contract is from date of Contract to March 31, 2027 inclusive. Site Visit. a. Optional Work Site Visit. Canada recommends that the Offeror attend the site visit. An optional site visit will be held at 442 ave des Cordillères on September 3, 2026 beginning at 9 am EDT, in Parks Canada Beauport Warehouse. b. Communication with Contracting Authority. Clarifications or Changes. Canada will amend the solicitation of offers to reflect clarifications and changes resulting from the site visit. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Corelands Maintenance Management Services
description: The NCC is seeking Maintenance Management Services with the objective of supporting high standards of service excellence at the best cost. The NCC manages contracts which provide high quality Maintenance services for the Commission’s corelands. The overall objectives of the Maintenance practices are to ensure public health and safety, protect and preserve assets and provide for an enjoyable experience of NCC sites in keeping with their key role as part of the Nation’s Capital.

The objectives of this requirement are to: 1. Support the improvement of the design, usability, and accessibility of TEA’s digital products through the application of recognized user experience (UX) principles, standards, and best practices, as required by the specific tasks identified under this Statement of Work, in support of internal users and external stakeholders. 2. title: NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSULTANT SERVICES
description: Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is calling for abbreviated proposals from consulting firms to establish a Source List (SL) to provide “as and when required” the following professional services at various locations in Alberta, Saskatchewan & Manitoba. Information provided by the Proponents will be evaluated using the established criteria in the RFAP. The SL will be for a period of three (3) years with a maximum estimated value of $7,500,000.00. If mutually agreeable between the Consultant and DCC, the SL may be extended for up to two (2) additional one (1) year periods and increased in the order of $5,000,000.00 anytime. Commissions under the SL are expected to be valued between $45,000.00 and $200,000.00; the maximum value of a commission under the SL is $500,000.00. Refer to the RFAP document for additional information. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Chapter Nineteen of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). Firms that consider themselves qualified to provide these services are invited to submit their Abbreviated Proposals through the MERX Electronic Bidding System on or before the closing date and time indicated on the Electronic Bidding System. The selected consultant will be required to hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS) security clearance issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).  Details concerning the Security Requirements for this project are identified in the RFAP documents. Questions regarding this solicitation are to be directed ONLY to the point of contact identified in this advertisement.  Proponents who address their questions to anyone other than the point of contact during the solicitation period may, for that reason alone, be disqualified. title: ET025-270110 - PIDS, FAAS Integration and Installation of IDS & MDS – RFP
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. CSC requires this project to address critical upgrades to Stony Mountain Institution’s security infrastructure to ensure enhanced perimeter protection and compliance with CSC’s Electronic Security Systems (ESS) National Standards for Graphical User Interfaces (GUI). The scope of the project includes but is not limited to: Integration of new and existing PIDS and FAAS equipment and systems into existing PIDS PSMS (Perimeter Security Management System) and FAAS ISMS(Interior Security Management System), at the SMI Institution, ensuring proper functionality and reliability of both PIDS and FAAS systems during and after integration, so that all integrated hardware and software, and equipment meet or exceed manufacturer specifications, CSC specifications and applicable standards, with system performance maintained or improved in terms of accuracy, response, and reliability. These systems must be presented to the operator through a touchscreen graphical user interface that integrates and manages the institution’s Electronic Security Systems. Replacement of ergonomic redevelopment of the physical MCCP user station will be required; and Design and installation of new Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Motion Detection Systems (MDS). Provision of associated professional services, including site investigation, assessment, detailed design, and construction support, in accordance with the Terms of Reference. See the Terms of Reference for more details.

description: The purpose of this Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of firms that possess the expertise to successfully complete and perform the requirements described herein. Furthermore, this effort seeks to address any questions, recommendations, or concerns from Industry. The information gathered will assist the Government in ensuring there is adequate competition among a potential pool of responsible contractors. Prior Government contract work is not required for submitting a response under this announcement. Please refer to the attached Sources Sought documentation for the updated details of this action. The Capabilities Statement requested for this Sources Sought is not intended to be a Request for Proposal (RFP) nor an Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. It is intended to request statements that thoroughly demonstrate interested companies existing expertise and experience (or developed plans for such) in relation to the areas specified herein. Any commercial brochures or currently existing marketing material may be submitted alongside the Capabilities Statement. Submission of a Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. All interested contractors should submit responses via email by 1000 hours Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on 22 Sep 2026. Submit responses and information to Elena.N.Shapovalova@usace.army.mil and Eric.L.Caruso@usace.army.mil. No hard copies will be accepted.

title: Blade Maintenance Stands
description: The basis of award will be low price. The Government intends to evaluate offers and award a contract without discussions with Offerors. Therefore, the Offerors initial offer should contain the Offerors best terms. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions, if necessary and deemed appropriate by the Contracting Officer. The Government may reject any or all offers if such action is in the public interest, accept other than the lowest offer, and waive informalities and minor irregularities in offers received. The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote is the lowest price that meets the requirements set forth in the Specifications. In accordance with RFO FAR 12.205(a), FAR Part 9, and DFARS 204.76, award will only be made to an offeror determined responsible, possessing an active SAM.gov registration, and demonstrating acceptable risk in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). Offerors are not required to submit past performance documentation. An offeror with an unsatisfactory SPRS score, delinquent delivery history, or adverse supply chain risk may be determined non-responsible and ineligible for award. All quotes will be reviewed and ensure that it meets the minimum requirements against the technical specifications provided below. To be eligible for award, a quote must satisfy all stated requirements set forth in the specifications; those that do not will be considered non-responsive. Because the Government intends to award without discussions, offerors are encouraged to submit their most competitive pricing and information in their response that meets the minimum set forth requirements in their initial response. This is a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) helicopter blade maintenance stands. This acquisition is conducted under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Commercial Items. The provisions of FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors--Commercial Items, apply to this solicitation. All responses are due by 22 September 2026 at 0900.

title: SyncPoint Pre-Solicitation Notice
description: Description of Requirement The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), PAE Maritime, intends to award a sole-source contract to Pioneering Evolution LLC, Arlington, VA, for the implementation, deployment, and support of SyncPoint � a commercial web-based program and financial management platform built on the proprietary SyncCore modular architecture. SyncPoint modernizes and unifies program planning, budgeting, execution oversight, and financial traceability for Program Management Offices (PMOs), Budget and Financial Managers (BFMs), Assistant Program Managers (APMs), and other stakeholders across the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) lifecycle. The platform replaces fragmented legacy tools with a single environment providing end-to-end visibility from POM planning through task execution, obligation tracking, G-Invoicing validation, and audit-ready financial reporting. Authority for Other Than Full and Open Competition This action is being pursued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1) and FAR 6.302-1 (�Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements�). Pioneering Evolution LLC is the only responsible source possessing the requisite proprietary technical data, source code, SyncCore architecture, design knowledge, resources, and experience to perform the required enhancements, integrations, and implementation without unacceptable delay. Notice of Intent This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement that clearly demonstrates the ability to meet the full requirement (including access to or rights in equivalent proprietary architecture/source code and the ability to deliver without the 18�24 month delay). Capability statements must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer no later than the response date listed above. Responses will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. If no capability statements are received that demonstrate the ability of another source to satisfy the requirement without unacceptable delay or cost, the Government will proceed with the sole-source award to Pioneering Evolution LLC. A Justification and Approval (J&A) documenting the basis for other than full and open competition will be prepared and, as required, made publicly available in accordance with FAR 6.305.

title: Electrophoresis CPT
description: Electrophoresis CPT Sources Sought Notice This notice is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an invitation for bid, request for quotation, request for proposal, or as an obligation of the government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice will be used for informational purposes only. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs from the government will arise as a result from a response to this announcement. No contract will be awarded from this notice. The information requested in this notice will be used to determine if there are sufficient socioeconomic small business concerns that are capable of performing the work described for the requirement. The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 17 is seeking sources for the following procurement: Electrophoresis CPT; Contractor shall provide a fully automated, gel electrophoresis instrument that can perform both serum and urine electrophoresis (SPEP/UPEP), immunofixation (SIFE/UIFE) and Immunotyping (IT) to identify monoclonal and polyclonal gammopathies for the Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Service of the South Texas Veterans Health Care System (STVHCS), Audie L. Murphy Memorial VA Hospital, located at 7400 Merton Minter Blvd., San Antonio, TX 78229. See attached Statement of Work. BACKGROUND South Texas Veterans Health Care System Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Services (P&LMS) 7400 Merton Minter Blvd. San Antonio, TX 78229 DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES The South Texas Veterans Health Care System (STVHCS) has a continued need for Serum and Urine Protein Electrophoresis, IFE, and IT instrumentation. The contractor shall provide a fully automated, gel electrophoresis instrument that can perform both serum and urine electrophoresis (SPEP/UPEP), immunofixation (SIFE/UIFE) and Immunotyping (IT) to identify monoclonal and polyclonal gammopathies. The Sebia instruments Capillarys and Hydrasys have been in use in the STVHCS Chemistry Laboratory 2016. See Price/Cost Schedule and Attachment A within the Statement of Work (SOW) for lists of estimated testing needs. (Quantities are estimates only). See attached SOW for the performance requirements. RESPONSE If interested, please provide the following information in a response: 1. Name of Company 2. Point of Contact; name, phone number and email address 3. SAM UEI # or DUNS number 4. Company socio-economic status (i.e., Small Business, SDVOSB/VOSB) 5. Capability Statement The information provided in a response to this notice may be used in developing an acquisition approach. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking any proprietary or competitive sensitive information that is provided in a response. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform must respond to the notice to be considered by 10:00 AM CST, September 22, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to Jose.Campa@va.gov. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions.

description: The U.S. Embassy in Bern, Switzerland invites qualified vendors to participate in a solicitation for temporary residential furniture rental and welcome kit services for government?leased residences in Bern and the surrounding areas. title: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta
description: This requirement is for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. This requirement is open only to those Supply Arrangement Holders under EW479-162880 who can perform the services in the geographical location of Alberta. The requirement is intended to result in the award of one (1) contract. The following Supply Arrangement Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: Stericycle Aevitas Clean Harbors Canada Inc. and Affiliated Companies GFL Environmental Inc. KBL Environmental Ltd. Shield Specialize Emergency Services Inc. Veolia es Canada Services Industriels Inc. Miller Environmental SUMAS Environmental Services Quest Disposal & Recycling Environmental 360 Solutions Description of the Requirement: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) K Division, Real Property and Asset Management has a requirement for the cleaning, removal, packing, disposal and/or recycling of hazardous waste materials from four RCMP Indoor Firing ranges located in Edmonton, Red Deer, Edson and St. Paul, Alberta. Level of Security Requirement: Resource Minimum Security Level Required: RCMP Facility Access Level 2 with Escort (FA2) Applicable Trade Agreements: Canada Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Columbia Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be for one year from date of contract award inclusive, with the irrevocable option to extend the term of the Contract by up to three additional one year periods under the same conditions. Estimated Level of Effort: The estimated level of effort of the contract, per year and across all 4 locations, will be: 10 times per year : Using steel rod, check the depth of rubber pellets from surface of trap to rigid steps of the bullet trap structure or new lead buildup in the middle of trap and its both corners. Add rubber pellets into bullet trap to maintain 600mm (24 inches) depth. Refill the trap hopper with new rubber pellets. Rake rubber pellets to cover rubber membrane at the back of the trap with rubber pellets. Level rubber berm surface to make proper slope. 5 times per year: Fix, patch, and/or flip rubber curtains if applicable 4 times per year: Replacement of rubber curtains or panels if applicable 4 times per year: Lead mining of the bullet trap system 4 times per year: Deep cleaning of firing range, range walls 1.8m AFF, training gear (e.g., target holders, First Air kit, etc.), all horizontal surfaces, control and gun cleaning rooms, floors, HEPA vacuum inside filter sections of supply and exhaust units 5 times per year: Replacement of pre-filters for exhaust ventilation unit HEPA filters replacement must be coordinated with Project Authority and to be done every 5 years (for Edson, St. Paul, and Red Deer sites), and every 4 years (Edmonton HQ) The estimated level of effort provided is for bid evaluated price determination purposes only. Their inclusion does not represent a commitment by Canada that Canada’s future usage of the services described in the bid solicitation will be consistent with this data. Solicitation Number: M5000-25-2334/A Contracting Authority: Sheena Simonson Phone Number: 306-515-1653 E-Mail: sheena.simonson@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Any supplier that wishes to submit a request to be a Supply Arrangement Holder for hazardous waste disposal services may do so by responding to the Request for Supply Arrangement (RFSA) with the solicitation number EW479-162880 on https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. title: Strengthening Carbon Market Readiness and Article 6 Operationalisation in Cameroon
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the Government of Cameroon. Cameroon, situated within the Congo Basin and home to significant forest carbon resources, is seeking to strengthen its readiness to participate in high-integrity international carbon markets, including Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), and voluntary carbon markets. While the country has considerable potential to generate climate finance through carbon markets and support implementation of its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), key legal, institutional, and operational gaps continue to constrain effective participation. This assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to support the Government of Cameroon in establishing the governance frameworks, institutional arrangements, and regulatory systems required to operationalise carbon market participation. Working closely with relevant government institutions, including the Ministry of Environment, Nature Protection and Sustainable Development (MINEPDED), the Ministry of Forestry and Wildlife (MINFOF), the Ministry of Finance (MINFI), and other key stakeholders, the project will strengthen carbon market governance, Article 6 implementation readiness, project approval systems, and institutional coordination mechanisms. Key outputs are expected to include a comprehensive carbon market readiness assessment, a carbon market governance framework defining the roles and responsibilities of key institutions, operational procedures for Article 6 participation and Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), a national carbon project approval system, and a structured capacity-building programme for government counterparts. The project will also support the integration of gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) considerations, safeguarding measures, and benefit-sharing approaches within carbon market governance arrangements. The project aims to strengthen Cameroon's ability to participate credibly and effectively in international carbon markets, mobilise climate finance, enhance institutional capacity, create an enabling environment for private sector investment, and support the delivery of national climate and sustainable development objectives. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk.

title: Bangladesh Carbon Market Governance & Readiness Sprint
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation. Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

title: Giant Voice Replacement
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The 87th Communications Squadron (CS) Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey is procuring a new requirement to engineer, Design, Furnish, Install, and Test (EDFI&T) a turnkey Giant Voice (GV) System at Joint-Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey (JB-MDL NJ). The current GV system consists of forty-two (42) outdoor GV poles (i.e., towers) that span over three joint base areas: McGuire, Dix, Ranges, and Lakehurst. This project will require installation of Giant Voice equipment for interoperability and compatibility with the AtHoc alert system and achieve uniformity for the whole JB-MDL GV system. The new GV system shall provide emergency messages, intelligible voice, tones, and pre-recorded alert notifications for the specified critical locations on JB-MDL NJ. It shall be able to communicate over the existing Radio Frequency (RF) communications infrastructure. The new stand-alone GV system shall provide sufficient intelligible voice coverage with real-time emergency alerting messages and accurate system health activities. Please see attached SOO for more information. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist, Noah Whiting at Noah.Whiting.1@us.af.mil, and the Contracting Officer, Lizbette Zalybniuk, at Lizbette.Zalybniuk.1@us.af.mil no later than 11 September 2026. ***PLEASE NOTE: There will be a site-visit associated with this requirement. title: BJS-Law Enforcement Calls for Service Data Platform
description: BJS-LAW ENFORCEMENT CALLS FOR SERVICE DATA PLATFORM This Request for Information (RFI) Notice is issued for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation for proposals. See the attached RFI for additional information. The U.S. Department of Justice/ Office of Justice Programs/ Bureau of Justice Statistics (USDOJ/ OJP/ BJS) is exploring the development of a national measure of law enforcement workload and activity that includes criminal and non-criminal police-public engagement. The concept of a national law enforcement calls for service (CFS) data platform is to establish a uniform, publicly available, event-based collection of law enforcement CFS captured in computer-aided dispatch (CAD) systems. BJS is seeking to understand the technical solutions that can automate the retrieval and standardization of information captured in CAD and can transform that information into an analyzable data system with uniform data elements and values. The Government retains ownership to software and application tools; upon completion this contract all information will be turned over to the U.S. Government and is U.S. Government property. The identified questions are to encourage competition and exchanges of information. Any voluntary response received will be reviewed to assist the Government in arriving at the most suitable approach. The Government is seeking responses to this RFI that describes vendors� existing capabilities. Small Business Participation: This RFI is issued on an unrestricted basis (Full and Open) to maximize industry responses. The Government highly encourages submissions from all business sizes and socioeconomic categories (e.g., Small Business, SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone). Infrastructure Assessment: Vendor shall simulate the realistic threat exploitation techniques within the legacy, existing, and emerging software system's cybersecurity in the mission context of the representative operating environment. Vendor shall apply the cybersecurity testing process with blue teams of Government and Vendor equivalent organizations and red teams of the certified Government and Vendor equivalent organizations during Developmental/Operational Test & Evaluation (D/O T&E).The Blue team assesses the operational network vulnerability with findings for the independent technical review of the network security posture and implements the mitigation techniques for integration into the community security solution to increase the cybersecurity readiness posture. The Blue teams evaluate the security threats/risks in the operating environment and study the network environment and its current state of security readiness. The Red teams simulate the potential adversary's exploitation capabilities against an enterprise's security posture to enhance the enterprise IA/Cybersecurity via demonstration of the impacts of the successful attacks and the needed countermeasure by the blue teams in the operational environment. This action will require TSI/SCI, but future work related to this action may require a TS/SCI with Counterintelligence Polygraph (TS/SCI w/CI Poly) clearance. The security requirements are IAW the attached DD Form 254, Security Classification Specification. Personnel must perform within the security limitations of AR 381-10, USSID 18, and other security regulations. Any vendor personnel that will need access to SIPRNet terminals will require a TS/SCI clearance because all SIPRNet terminals are in Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIFs) Security Boundary Clarification: The vendor shall understand and apply all applicable security classification guidance. Users should notify the originator if information indicates a need to update the guidance. Classification determinations remain the responsibility of the Government Contracting Agency (GCA). The Contract Security Classification Specification (DD254) is required for performance on a classified contract. Infrastructure for Cyber Operations: The vendor shall leverage infrastructure as code such as terraform or related for deployments and cloud management. Cyber-Network Architecture: develop, maintain, and update documentation which includes Standard Operating Procedures, System Architecture Guides, Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), Install Guides, and Department of Defense Architectural Framework (DoDAF) diagrams for all related system and hardware configurations adhering to organizational templated and policies quarterly. The vendor shall leverage cross-domain solutions for implementation for tempest hardening and significant equipment installations. The vendor shall not implement solutions that have licenses or incur additional costs without written approval from the Government stakeholders, COR, and ACOR. Post-RFI Events: Following the evaluation of RFI responses, the Government anticipates hosting an Industry Day to facilitate open exchanges of information and provide further program details. A separate announcement containing registration, scheduling, and security clearance instructions for the Industry Day will be published on SAM.gov. The feasibility of conducting associated physical site visits is currently under evaluation and will be announced at a later date, if applicable. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Vendors may only submit one (1) submission per CAGE code. Interested sources are requested to submit a response of no more than five (5) pages, written in Times New Roman font of 12-point size or larger. Times New Roman of 10-point size is acceptable for graphics, tables, or exhibits. Responses must be in either Microsoft Word or character recognized and searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). If your company has different business sectors which hold different CAGE codes, each sector may submit a response. In addition, each CAGE code must provide separate facility clearance documentation which will not count against the 5 page limit. If teaming, use the Prime Vendor's CAGE code in the response. Submission of proprietary and other sensitive information must be marked and identified with disposition instructions. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations and requirements. title: Platform One Solutions Marketplace (P1SM)/Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)
description: Platform One, with support from its marketplace manager, The Applied Research Institute (ARI), is initiating a long-term, open call for solutions to support the DoD in quickly delivering high-quality, secure software with accelerated delivery times. The solutions will support or enable the delivery of resilient software capability at the speed of relevance, ensuring the DoD remains agile and responsive to emerging threats and opportunities. Specifically, Platform One seeks to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technological advancements. Innovative solutions encompass technologies, processes, or methods (including research and development) that are newly developed or applied in a novel way as of the submission date. This initiative, entitled the �Platform One Solutions Marketplace� (P1SM) will solicit, collect, assess, and curate hardware, software, or service solutions and make those solutions available through rapid acquisition pathways. This approach aims to foster innovation and expedite the integration of cutting-edge technologies into the DoD's operational framework, enhancing its ability to deliver software at the speed of relevance.

title: Giant Voice Replacement
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The 87th Communications Squadron (CS) Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey is procuring a new requirement to engineer, Design, Furnish, Install, and Test (EDFI&T) a turnkey Giant Voice (GV) System at Joint-Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey (JB-MDL NJ). The current GV system consists of forty-two (42) outdoor GV poles (i.e., towers) that span over three joint base areas: McGuire, Dix, Ranges, and Lakehurst. This project will require installation of Giant Voice equipment for interoperability and compatibility with the AtHoc alert system and achieve uniformity for the whole JB-MDL GV system. The new GV system shall provide emergency messages, intelligible voice, tones, and pre-recorded alert notifications for the specified critical locations on JB-MDL NJ. It shall be able to communicate over the existing Radio Frequency (RF) communications infrastructure. The new stand-alone GV system shall provide sufficient intelligible voice coverage with real-time emergency alerting messages and accurate system health activities. Please see attached SOO for more information. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist, Noah Whiting at Noah.Whiting.1@us.af.mil, and the Contracting Officer, Lizbette Zalybniuk, at Lizbette.Zalybniuk.1@us.af.mil no later than 11 September 2026. ***PLEASE NOTE: There will be a site-visit associated with this requirement. The site visit will be held on location at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst on 9 September 2026 at 1000. Please contact Contract Administrator, Noah Whiting, at Noah.whiting.1@us.af.mil to be added to our EAL by the deadline of 1400 on 02 September 2026. Please note that all individuals on EAL and planning to enter JB MDL will undergo a background check. Admittance to Government Facilities will depend on the outcome of the same.***

title: Test Pit and Soil Borings
description: INTRODUCTION: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe) is providing support to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Targeted Brownfields Assessments (TBA) Program. As part of this effort, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) that includes a requirement for the advancement of test pits and soil borings will be conducted at the Royal Electric Yard (the Site) located at 7512 Main St, Sykesville, Maryland 21784. A 2026 Phase I ESA conducted at the Site identified historic automotive junking activities and small, partially buried piles of automotive debris in the northern, wooded portion of the property. It was determined that there is a likely presence of hazardous substances or petroleum products associated with former automotive operations including used oils, brake and hydraulic fluids, gasoline and diesel fuels, mercury switches, asbestos brake parts, refrigerants, metals, batteries, and antifreezes. A Phase II ESA was recommended to determine if these historical activities have impacted the Site. As part of this Phase II ESA, test pits and soil borings will be collected to assess any impacts from potential contaminants of concern. The property is an approximately 4.1-acre parcel (Maryland Tax Account Number #05- 072190) located adjacent to Sykesville�s historic main street district. Sykesville is located within Carroll County. Major features at the property include a warehouse, gravel parking lot, and access road in the southern portion, and an unmaintained wooded area in the northern portion. Due to a pending sale of the Site, the primary area of interest is limited to the northern half of the property. The site generally slopes to the south, with the wooded area alternating between relatively flat terraces and steeper slopes. A review of the Natural Resources Conservation Service National Cooperative Soil Survey shows that the Site�s soil primarily consists of silt-loam, loam, and complexes. The area just south of the warehouse is underlain by Glenville-urban land-Udorthents complex, which indicates possible presence of fill. The Site location and the boundaries of the investigation are included in the Field Sampling Plan, provided as SOW Attachment 1. TASKS TO BE PERFORMED: The Contractor must be a Maryland licensed driller and shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State and local requirements as well as applicable Volpe Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs, see SOW Attachment VII). Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. A schedule for these tasks is provided in Section 4. a) Work Plan The Contractor shall attend a kickoff meeting with Volpe Center representatives within five (5) business days of the contract award. During the meeting, Contractor tasks and schedules will be discussed. Prior to the meeting, the contractor shall thoroughly review any Government-furnished information provided to them. Within ten (10) business days of the kickoff meeting, the Contractor shall submit the following in writing to the Volpe Center as part of a brief Work Plan: A description of Contractor�s approach to the tasks as outlined in the following subsections, including the personnel, machinery, and other equipment that is planned to be used. Due to terrain and vegetation conditions at the site, the government prefers that the smallest equipment capable of completing the tasks be used. The Contractor is responsible for the security of equipment staged onsite, if applicable. A proposed schedule of the remaining Contractor tasks as outlined in the following subsections. A description of any required permits needed to perform the work. The Contractor shall be responsible for identifying and obtaining those permits. Copies of the permits shall be submitted to the Volpe Center prior to the start of Site work. If no permits are required, justification for this should be cited. Site Safety and Health Plan, which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed and a Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards the site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. The Volpe Center will review the Work Plan within five (5) business days of receipt and submit any necessary revisions before approving. If revisions are needed, a revised Work Plan should be returned to the Volpe Center within five (5 business days) of receiving comments. b) Sample Location Access and Vegetation Clearing Some sample (test pit or soil boring) locations are in a wooded area where vegetation and uneven terrain need to be navigated. The Contractor shall clear vegetation and be prepared to access all proposed locations for the geophysical survey, test pitting, and/or soil boring activities described in the following tasks. Volpe visited all sample locations in August 2026 to assess vegetation conditions. At some locations, weeds and grasses up to approximately knee-height, fallen logs up 6 to 12 inches in diameter, and overhead vines and branches were encountered. The contractor shall be prepared to clear vegetation to the extent that equipment can access each sample location from the parking lot and that there is sufficient space to operate the equipment. Based on the conditions observed by Volpe at the site, vegetation is anticipated to be able to be removed by suggested methods such as chainsaw, clippers, weed trimmer, mini-excavator, and hand-removal. No removal of established trees or grading is expected to be needed. Cut materials may be left onsite. Photos of the vegetation conditions observed in August 2026 are included as SOW Attachment 3. During this visit, sample locations were marked with GPS (and may vary from the Field Sampling Plan figures). A PDF file of these field-marked locations is included as SOW Attachment X. c) Geophysical Survey The Contractor shall conduct a geophysical survey to identify potential buried debris stemming from historical automotive junking operations at the Site. The geophysical survey shall be completed by a person qualified and experienced in geophysical surveying and shall incorporate the use of appropriate geophysical sensing equipment (e.g., electromagnetic conductivity, ground penetrating radar, and/or magnetometry) to detect potential buried debris and identify its anticipated depth and extent. The survey will be conducted in approximately 25 ft. x 25 ft. areas centered around each of the six proposed test pit areas, which are targeted to areas with observed surface and/or partially buried debris. These areas are subject to relocation based on site conditions. Within 10 days of completing the survey, the Contractor shall prepare and submit a brief geophysical survey report that shall include a summary of the work performed and equipment used, a description of the findings, a map of surveyed areas and identified anomalies, and photographs of the surveyed areas. d) Utility Clearance The Contractor shall notify Call-Before-You-Dig (811) services in sufficient time before the commencement of soil boring or test pitting activities. The Contractor shall follow all applicable laws to complete this notification. A copy of the notification ticket shall be submitted to the Volpe Center prior to beginning the following tasks. In addition to Call-Before-You-Dig notification, the Contractor shall utilize ground penetrating radar and electromagnetic technologies (or equivalent equipment) to verify Call-Before-You-Dig markings and to complete a private utility locate to clear each of the six proposed test pit locations and ten proposed soil boring locations. If obstructions are present that require a proposed test pit or soil boring to be moved, the Volpe Center will work with a Contractor to identify and clear an alternate location. title: Various Licenses and Cables for FEMA Region VI
description: The purpose of this RFQ is to solicit quotes for Shure ANX4 Incremental Channel Expansion Licenses and UniFi Indoor Cat6A CMP cable for FEMA Region VI Federal Regional Center and the Texas Room located in the Russell Newman Building. This is an open market RFQ under NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services, Information Technology Value Added Resellers, with a size standard of 150 employees. Award will be made on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. All licenses must be valid OEM or publisher-authorized entitlements. All cable supplies must be new, genuine OEM products. All quoted items must be TAA compliant, as applicable. The range of affordability is $47,000.00. This amount is for affordability purposes only and is not a ceiling or floor. Quoters shall provide an itemized quote for each CLIN, including product description, manufacturer, part number, quantity, unit price, extended price, and warranty or license support information. Questions must be emailed to Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov by 12:00 PM CT on September 16, 2026. Quoters must reference RFQ 70FBR626Q00000041 in all correspondence. Phone calls will not be accepted. Invoices may be submitted only after all required items and license/support information have been delivered and accepted by the Government. The nonmanufacturer rule is not separately stated in the RFQ. The Government confirms that the nonmanufacturer rule does not apply to this acquisition because the RFQ is at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. All other terms and conditions of the RFQ remain unchanged, including the requirements for new, genuine OEM products and valid publisher-authorized license entitlements, authorized reseller or distributor documentation, delivery, warranty/support, and all applicable RFQ requirements. A non-TAA country of origin, by itself, will not make a CLIN technically unacceptable, provided the quoted item otherwise meets all RFQ requirements, including requirements for new, genuine, authorized, non-counterfeit, non-gray-market products and valid license entitlements. title: The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times)
description: Description This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or questions. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain knowledge and information for project planning purposes. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The NIH seeks information on technologies and capabilities to further the objectives of the Data COUNTS program. The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times) effort is built on collaboration between patients and advocates, government, health systems, technology companies, and the private sector. The Data COUNTS program enables the NIH�s Real-World Data initiative and will provide high quality, standardized data that is provenanced and available through approved access to the research community. The contemplated capability will initially perform requested and approved extraction from Healthcare Partner EMR systems and should be modular and extensible to other authorized source systems such as laboratory information systems, pharmacy information systems, picture archiving and communication systems, vendor-neutral archives, and specialty systems. The Data COUNTS program requires that source data, and source provenance metadata, permissions, and source ontology fields will be preserved without modification or loss. This program will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Technical Requirements of Interest: Address availability and technologies that enable the following features: A durable, Healthcare Partner Leave Behind Technology capability that remains at the Healthcare Partner site after contract completion and can be operated by trained staff without ongoing involvement. The technology should be available and free for use by Healthcare Partners while in the Data COUNTS program. Describe any installation and configuration documentation, operational runbooks, site-controlled credential-transfer procedures, documented dependencies, major-release update procedures, and training that enable independent site operations. Deep query for approved extraction from Healthcare Partner electronic medical records (EMR) systems and other authorized source systems. Capture timestamps and provenance for all data at extraction and maintain an immutable provenance chain. The architecture consumes a machine-readable, version-controlled, authorized, and approved Data Request Specification defining cohort logic, requested source systems, data domains and fields, date range, full or incremental extraction mode, refresh cadence, and applicable authorization and permission rules. Describe how the solution validates data availability against the specification, identifies unavailable or ambiguous fields, avoids silent substitutions, associates the request identifier with each batch and output, and supports reproducible reruns when source data have not changed. An initial automated data quality check validating completeness, uniqueness, data types, date sequencing, and records-per-patient. All anomalies must be reported before any permitted corrections are applied. Sourced data will not be modified De-identification per 45 CFR �164.514(b): remove all 18 direct identifiers; document a consistent de-identification pathway; and apply a per-patient date-shifting specification that preserves temporal order. Privacy Preserving Record Linkage (PPRL) tokenization capabilities for cross-site linkage using an approved, on-premises within the institutional trust boundary PPRL platform that generates consistent, irreversible patient tokens. Describe validation and Healthcare Partner approval before the first live transmission. Describe how token consistency is achieved across independently deployed, site-local PPRL instances, without introducing a shared trust boundary outside the Healthcare Partner site. Describe how the solution preserves all source provenance metadata, permissions information, and ontology fields (e.g. SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, RxNorm, UCUM, etc.) without modification or loss, excluding authorized de-identification transformations performed under Section 4. The DSP will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Metadata must be additive, clearly identified, and each output value must be traceable to the source and authorized transformation. Describe how the solution consumes authoritative eligibility supplied by the Healthcare Partner and applies it before transmission; records the governing authorization or permission version for each dataset; distinguish cohort exclusions from permission exclusions; and apply revocations so that revoked records are absent from all subsequent refreshes. Describe how the solution generates full and incremental extracts; maintains stable patient tokens; creates unique snapshot and refresh IDs; supports idempotent reruns; identifies added, updated, deleted, merged, unmerged, corrected, and late-arriving records to the appropriate refresh cycle. Workflow Integrity & Processing Audit: maintain audit records for each stage; timestamp, stage ID, batch ID, record counts, outcome, and reconciliation status. Failed reconciliations or incomplete processing stages must halt transmission until resolved or authorized for reprocessing. Security Posture: Describe the ability to attest to HIPAA Security Rule compliance as a Business Associate; Security Audit Logging to generate SIEM-compatible security logs for authentication, administrative actions, configuration changes, and security events. Record timestamp, user/service account, action, resource, and outcome. Security logs must be protected against unauthorized modification or deletion, and logging must be continuous. Defense-in-Depth Encryption: TLS 1.3 where supported; TLS 1.2 minimum for all data in transit,; application-level encryption of output files and VM-level encryption. Attack Surface Minimization with no unnecessary ports, services, or network listeners by default. The only authorized external connection is the outbound TLS path to the Data COUNT Program Also see Section 1 regarding on-site operation of Leave Behind Technology; this section addresses the boundary for identifiable data processing. Describe how identifiable processing is confined to the Healthcare Partner�s VM and institutional trust boundary; only de-identified, tokenized output is transmitted for the Data COUNTS program; access is integrated with Healthcare Partner identity and access controls and is site-managed and logged; and the deployed solution does not include or permit contractor credentials, contractor remote-access pathways, or contractor remote-management capabilities. Describe supported performance at baseline, 2X, and 5X expected workloads and identify assumed data volumes, throughput, processing time, and Healthcare Partner CPU, memory, storage, network and staffing requirements. Describe how the solution can reliably package, transmit, reconcile, and retry deliveries to the TDB, including package, schema versioning, and error resolution. Business Information Requested Please provide information on the following: Details on which capabilities are able to be met Clarification on which features are commercial off-the-shelf (COTS), and which features would be considered minor modifications, and which features would be considered custom development features Billing model and pricing structure and any additional features and their subsequent costs Experience with successful implementation capabilities and list of healthcare partners Experience of similar work with Federal Government agencies Experience of similar work with industries or non-profit organizations Business size and status Response Format: Responses must be submitted by October 1, 2026, 3:00 Eastern Standard Time to DataCounts@nih.gov with the subject line Company Name RFI Response. Responses must be submitted in PDF o

title: Occupational Medical Services (OMS)
description: 1. Purpose The NIH, on behalf of the ORS Division of Occupational Health and Safety, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of performing Occupational Medical Services and to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether the requirement can be set aside for small business concerns under a socioeconomic program. This notice specifically seeks to determine the availability and capability of: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) HUBZone Small Businesses Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) / Economically Disadvantaged WOSB (EDWOSB) Other small business concerns The Government will use responses to this notice to make decisions regarding set-aside determinations consistent with applicable regulations and Department policy. No award will be made from this notice. 2. Background NIH DOHS operates an Occupational Medical Service that provides work-related medical care and counseling to the NIH workforce, including emergency medical care, pre-placement medical evaluations, medical care for occupational injuries and illnesses, work-related immunizations and health surveillance programs, and employee assistance/counseling services. Performance supports a biomedical research community with potential chemical, biological, animal, physical, and radiological workplace hazards in addition to typical occupational hazards. This is a follow-on to an existing requirement. The Government is considering a single-award, cost-reimbursement (cost-plus-fixed-fee) contract with a base period and option periods, subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS). 3. Anticipated Scope of Work (Summary) The Contractor would be expected to furnish qualified personnel, materials, equipment, and services to perform, at a minimum: Emergency and urgent medical care for work-related conditions Pre-placement and periodic medical evaluations Work-related immunizations and travel medicine Medical surveillance programs (e.g., animal exposure, respiratory/asbestos, TB, hearing conservation, and related biomedical-hazard programs) Employee Assistance Program (EAP) counseling services Clinical operations across multiple fixed sites, with a limited mobile/traveling component (e.g., seasonal flu clinics) Associated quality control/quality improvement, reporting, records management, and information-security/privacy compliance (moderate-impact PII/IT security) Anticipated performance locations include: Bethesda, MD; Frederick, MD; Baltimore, MD; Research Triangle Park, NC; and Hamilton, MT. (Respondents should indicate ability to staff all locations.) 4. Information Requested from Respondents Interested firms are requested to submit a capability statement, not to exceed [8�10] pages, addressing the items below. Marketing materials alone are not sufficient. A. Company Information Company name, UEI/SAM registration status, address, and point of contact (name, title, phone, email). Business size under NAICS 621498 (small or other than small). B. Socioeconomic Status - See Attachment 2. C. Capability and Experience A description of your firm's experience providing occupational medical, ambulatory/clinical, or comparable health services of similar size, scope, and complexity, preferably within the last five (5) years. For up to three (3) relevant contracts, provide: customer/agency, contract number, dollar value, period of performance, contract type, a brief scope description, and whether performed as prime or subcontractor. Experience providing services across multiple geographic locations concurrently. Experience with cost-reimbursement (CPFF) contracts, including whether your firm has an accounting system that has been determined adequate for cost-reimbursement contracts (e.g., by DCAA or a cognizant Federal agency), and the date/type of any such determination. Ability to recruit, credential, and retain licensed clinical staff (e.g., physicians, nurses, PAs, EAP counselors) for federal occupational health work. D. Small Business Participation If your firm is a small business, describe your ability to perform the primary and vital requirements of this effort and to comply with the applicable limitations on subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14) for a set-aside of this type. Indicate the percentage of the work your firm would self-perform. 5. Set-Aside Interest Statement To assist the Government's set-aside analysis, please state whether your firm intends to submit an offer if this requirement is issued as a set-aside under any of the following, and at a fair market price: (a) SDVOSB set-aside; (b) HUBZone set-aside; (c) WOSB/EDWOSB set-aside; (d) total small business set-aside. 6. Submission Instructions Submit capability statements electronically to Contracting Officer, Aytaj Vily, aytaj.vily@nih.gov no later than 9/22/2026 3:00 PM ET. Reference "Sources Sought � Occupational Medical Services (OMS)" in the subject line. Files should be in Microsoft Word or PDF format, [8�10] pages maximum, single-sided, minimum 11-point font. 7. Additional Notes This notice does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that the Government will issue a solicitation or award a contract. No solicitation document exists at this time. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding to this notice. Responses will be used for market research only and may inform the acquisition strategy, including the set-aside determination and NAICS assignment. Proprietary information should be clearly marked; the Government will protect such information to the extent permitted by law. All firms responding are advised that any resultant solicitation, if issued, will be posted on SAM.gov (www.sam.gov). It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor SAM.gov for any resulting solicitation. Respondents should ensure their SAM.gov registration and any applicable socioeconomic certifications are active and current.

title: Intent to Sole Source- Automated Blood Bank Instrumentation
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to QuidelOrtho Sales Company, LLC, located at 9975 Summers Ridge Road, San Diego, California, 92121. This proposed action is for automated blood bank instrumentation, reagents, consumables, and associated support for the 88th Medical Group Laboratory Flight at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB). This requirement is for a fully automated, continuous-access blood bank system integrated with current and future laboratory information systems, including MHS Genesis, together with the associated training, maintenance, repair, and reagent support necessary to maintain uninterrupted blood bank operations. Extensive market research was conducted to identify potential sources. Techniques included, but were not limited to, internet market research, review of similar procurements, input from Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), review of the Government�s minimum technical requirements, and a Sources Sought notice. The BPA justification states that no existing mandatory source has been identified that can satisfy the organization�s specific blood and blood product requirements. The WPAFB 88th Medical Group requires a blood bank instrumentation solution that meets the minimum technical requirements established in the Statement of Work (SOW). These requirements include a fully automated blood bank system using the required methodology, support for required blood bank testing on a single platform, integration capability with MHS Genesis, FDA-approved reagent kits, and instrument-specific reagents, controls, standards, and hardware from the manufacturer producing the instrument. Utilizing a system that does not meet these requirements would not satisfy the Government�s operational and patient care needs. title: The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times)
description: Description This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or questions. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain knowledge and information for project planning purposes. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The NIH seeks information on technologies and capabilities to further the objectives of the Data COUNTS program. The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times) effort is built on collaboration between patients and advocates, government, health systems, technology companies, and the private sector. The Data COUNTS program enables the NIH�s Real-World Data initiative and will provide high quality, standardized data that is provenanced and available through approved access to the research community. The contemplated capability will initially perform requested and approved extraction from Healthcare Partner EMR systems and should be modular and extensible to other authorized source systems such as laboratory information systems, pharmacy information systems, picture archiving and communication systems, vendor-neutral archives, and specialty systems. The Data COUNTS program requires that source data, and source provenance metadata, permissions, and source ontology fields will be preserved without modification or loss. This program will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Technical Requirements of Interest: Address availability and technologies that enable the following features: A durable, Healthcare Partner Leave Behind Technology capability that remains at the Healthcare Partner site after contract completion and can be operated by trained staff without ongoing involvement. The technology should be available and free for use by Healthcare Partners while in the Data COUNTS program. Describe any installation and configuration documentation, operational runbooks, site-controlled credential-transfer procedures, documented dependencies, major-release update procedures, and training that enable independent site operations. Deep query for approved extraction from Healthcare Partner electronic medical records (EMR) systems and other authorized source systems. Capture timestamps and provenance for all data at extraction and maintain an immutable provenance chain. The architecture consumes a machine-readable, version-controlled, authorized, and approved Data Request Specification defining cohort logic, requested source systems, data domains and fields, date range, full or incremental extraction mode, refresh cadence, and applicable authorization and permission rules. Describe how the solution validates data availability against the specification, identifies unavailable or ambiguous fields, avoids silent substitutions, associates the request identifier with each batch and output, and supports reproducible reruns when source data have not changed. An initial automated data quality check validating completeness, uniqueness, data types, date sequencing, and records-per-patient. All anomalies must be reported before any permitted corrections are applied. Sourced data will not be modified De-identification per 45 CFR �164.514(b): remove all 18 direct identifiers; document a consistent de-identification pathway; and apply a per-patient date-shifting specification that preserves temporal order. Privacy Preserving Record Linkage (PPRL) tokenization capabilities for cross-site linkage using an approved, on-premises within the institutional trust boundary PPRL platform that generates consistent, irreversible patient tokens. Describe validation and Healthcare Partner approval before the first live transmission. Describe how token consistency is achieved across independently deployed, site-local PPRL instances, without introducing a shared trust boundary outside the Healthcare Partner site. Describe how the solution preserves all source provenance metadata, permissions information, and ontology fields (e.g. SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, RxNorm, UCUM, etc.) without modification or loss, excluding authorized de-identification transformations performed under Section 4. The DSP will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Metadata must be additive, clearly identified, and each output value must be traceable to the source and authorized transformation. Describe how the solution consumes authoritative eligibility supplied by the Healthcare Partner and applies it before transmission; records the governing authorization or permission version for each dataset; distinguish cohort exclusions from permission exclusions; and apply revocations so that revoked records are absent from all subsequent refreshes. Describe how the solution generates full and incremental extracts; maintains stable patient tokens; creates unique snapshot and refresh IDs; supports idempotent reruns; identifies added, updated, deleted, merged, unmerged, corrected, and late-arriving records to the appropriate refresh cycle. Workflow Integrity & Processing Audit: maintain audit records for each stage; timestamp, stage ID, batch ID, record counts, outcome, and reconciliation status. Failed reconciliations or incomplete processing stages must halt transmission until resolved or authorized for reprocessing. Security Posture: Describe the ability to attest to HIPAA Security Rule compliance as a Business Associate; Security Audit Logging to generate SIEM-compatible security logs for authentication, administrative actions, configuration changes, and security events. Record timestamp, user/service account, action, resource, and outcome. Security logs must be protected against unauthorized modification or deletion, and logging must be continuous. Defense-in-Depth Encryption: TLS 1.3 where supported; TLS 1.2 minimum for all data in transit,; application-level encryption of output files and VM-level encryption. Attack Surface Minimization with no unnecessary ports, services, or network listeners by default. The only authorized external connection is the outbound TLS path to the Data COUNT Program Also see Section 1 regarding on-site operation of Leave Behind Technology; this section addresses the boundary for identifiable data processing. Describe how identifiable processing is confined to the Healthcare Partner�s VM and institutional trust boundary; only de-identified, tokenized output is transmitted for the Data COUNTS program; access is integrated with Healthcare Partner identity and access controls and is site-managed and logged; and the deployed solution does not include or permit contractor credentials, contractor remote-access pathways, or contractor remote-management capabilities. Describe supported performance at baseline, 2X, and 5X expected workloads and identify assumed data volumes, throughput, processing time, and Healthcare Partner CPU, memory, storage, network and staffing requirements. Describe how the solution can reliably package, transmit, reconcile, and retry deliveries to the TDB, including package, schema versioning, and error resolution. Business Information Requested Please provide information on the following: Details on which capabilities are able to be met Clarification on which features are commercial off-the-shelf (COTS), and which features would be considered minor modifications, and which features would be considered custom development features Billing model and pricing structure and any additional features and their subsequent costs Experience with successful implementation capabilities and list of healthcare partners Experience of similar work with Federal Government agencies Experience of similar work with industries or non-profit organizations Business size and status Response Format: Responses must be submitted by September 22, 2026, 3:00 Eastern Standard Time to DataCounts@nih.gov with the subject line Company Name RFI Response. Responses must be submitted in PD
